LASIK vs Contact Lenses – Which is Better for Students? | ASG Eye Hospital

Students today spend long hours studying, attending classes, using digital devices, and participating in sports or extracurricular activities. Clear vision is essential, making many students choose between contact lenses and LASIK surgery.

Contact lenses offer temporary vision correction, but they require daily cleaning, proper hygiene, and ongoing maintenance. Extended wear can sometimes lead to dryness, irritation, and an increased risk of eye infections.

LASIK surgery, on the other hand, provides long-term vision correction and reduces dependence on glasses or contact lenses. For eligible students with a stable eye prescription, 

LASIK offers several advantages:

• Freedom from daily lens maintenance
• No recurring costs for lenses and solutions
• Greater convenience during sports and activities
• Improved comfort during long study sessions
• Reduced dependence on vision correction accessories

Modern LASIK eye surgery uses advanced diagnostic technology to create personalized treatment plans with high precision and safety. Most students can return to their routine within a few days.

Best Eye Specialist for Retina Problems | ASG Eye Hospital

The retina plays a vital role in vision, yet many retinal conditions develop silently and may not show symptoms until significant damage has occurred. Early diagnosis by a retina specialist can help protect vision and improve treatment outcomes.

Warning signs that need immediate attention:

• Sudden flashes of light
• New or increasing floaters
• Blurred or distorted vision
• A dark curtain or shadow in vision
• Difficulty reading or recognising faces
• Sudden vision loss

Common retina disorders include diabetic retinopathy, retinal detachment, macular degeneration, macular holes, and retinal tears. Many of these conditions respond better when diagnosed and treated early.

At ASG Eye Hospital, advanced retinal imaging and modern diagnostic technology help specialists detect retinal problems accurately and recommend the most appropriate retina treatment.

Available treatment options may include:

• Retinal laser treatment
• Intravitreal injections
• Vitrectomy surgery
• Retinal detachment repair
• Ongoing retinal monitoring

Delaying treatment can increase the risk of permanent vision loss. If you notice any sudden changes in your eyesight, seeking prompt evaluation from a qualified retina specialist is essential.

Book your retina consultation at ASG Eye Hospital today and take the first step toward protecting your vision.

Diabetes can affect your eyesight without obvious warning signs. Many people with diabetic eye disease experience no symptoms until retinal damage has already begun. Regular eye examinations are essential for protecting long-term vision.

Common symptoms to watch for include:

• Blurred or fluctuating vision
• Floaters or dark spots
• Difficulty reading
• Distorted vision
• Poor night vision
• Sudden vision changes

One of the most common diabetes-related eye conditions is diabetic retinopathy, which affects the blood vessels in the retina. Early detection through retinal screening can help prevent serious vision complications.

Protect your eye health by:

• Monitoring blood pressure regularly
• Taking medications as prescribed
• Staying physically active
• Avoiding tobacco use
• Scheduling regular eye check-ups

I visited Dr. Hemant for blurred vision and unfortunately had a very disappointing experience.

Upon arrival, the assistant conducted a standard vision test and informed me that my vision was perfect as I was able to read even the smallest letters. A pressure test was also performed, and I was told that the results were normal.

After this, I was repeatedly asked whether anyone in my family had glaucoma. I clearly stated that no one in my family has a history of glaucoma. Despite being told that my initial tests appeared normal, I was advised to undergo additional tests costing approximately ₹2,400 each. After those tests, I was again informed that the reports looked normal, yet I was asked to undergo two more tests costing another ₹2,400 each because the doctor "wanted more clarity." At this stage, my bill had already reached around ₹11,600.

I requested to meet the doctor before proceeding further and was eventually allowed to do so. During the consultation, I felt that my concerns regarding blurred vision were not adequately addressed. When I repeatedly asked what was causing my symptoms, I was mostly told that I was anxious and overthinking. I was reassured that I would not go blind, but I did not receive a clear explanation of my diagnosis.

What confused me further was that I was prescribed Thyronorm 25 mcg despite informing the doctor that I do not have a thyroid condition. My thyroid reports were normal, yet I was advised to take the medication for two days without a clear explanation of why it was necessary.

I was then told to return after two days for pupil dilation and further examination, along with an additional consultation charge. I questioned why this could not be done during the same visit, especially after already undergoing multiple expensive tests, but no satisfactory explanation was provided.

The post-consultation experience was equally frustrating. The prescription did not mention when to take the prescribed medication, and I was advised to WhatsApp the doctor for clarification. Despite following up multiple times, I did not receive a timely response. I also requested copies of my reports but was told that the printer was not working. However, I observed other documents being printed during my visit. More than five days later, I still had not received all my reports as promised.

Another concern was the pricing of the tests. After my visit, I checked with other centres and found that similar tests are often charged between ₹900 and ₹1,200. This left me questioning why I was charged significantly higher amounts without a clear explanation.

I fully understand that specialist consultations and advanced diagnostics can be expensive when medically justified. However, as a patient, I felt pressured into undergoing multiple tests before receiving a proper explanation of my condition. The lack of transparency, poor communication, difficulty obtaining reports, and inadequate follow-up made this a very disappointing experience.

I hope this feedback encourages greater transparency, clearer communication with patients, and better post-consultation support in the future.

Understanding Cornea Transplant: Will Eye Color Change? 🤔

Considering a cornea transplant? A common question is whether the procedure will affect your eye color. Since only the central transparent tissue is replaced, your natural eye color, determined by the iris, typically remains the same. However, individual cases vary, so it's best to consult with an expert.

Meet Dr. Vinay Agrawal from Clear Vision Eye Centre, Santacruz West, who can guide you through the process and address your concerns about cornea transplants.

Book your consultation today!

Is a Cornea Transplant a Permanent Solution? (Get the Facts)

Considering a cornea transplant? It's natural to wonder if it's a "forever" fix.

The short answer is: For many people, yes, it can provide significantly improved vision for decades! However, "permanent" is a complex term in medicine. Here's what you need to know:

Is Glaucoma Hereditary? How to Protect Your Family’s Vision

Glaucoma is one of the most serious eye conditions because it can damage vision silently. In many cases, people do not notice symptoms in the early stages. By the time vision changes become obvious, some damage to the optic nerve may already be permanent.

If your parent, sibling, or close family member has glaucoma, you may wonder: Is glaucoma hereditary? The answer is yes. Glaucoma can run in families, and a family history of glaucoma is an important risk factor.

The good news is that early detection and regular monitoring can help protect your vision. The National Eye Institute explains that glaucoma can cause vision loss and blindness by damaging the optic nerve, but early treatment can often stop further damage and protect vision.

If glaucoma runs in your family, scheduling a comprehensive eye check-up with an experienced eye specialist is one of the most important steps you can take.

Is Glaucoma Hereditary?

Yes, glaucoma can be hereditary. Having a family history of glaucoma increases your risk, especially if a first-degree relative such as a parent, brother, sister, or child has been diagnosed.

A population-based study published in Archives of Ophthalmology found that first-degree relatives of people with glaucoma had a much higher lifetime risk of glaucoma compared with relatives of people without glaucoma. The study reported a risk ratio of 9.2 for glaucoma in relatives of glaucoma patients.

The cornea is the clear, dome-shaped front surface of the eye. It protects the eye from dust, germs, and injury, and it also helps focus light so you can see clearly. Because the cornea is exposed and highly sensitive, even a small scratch, infection, or swelling can cause significant discomfort.

Corneal problems should never be ignored. Some minor scratches heal quickly, but deeper injuries, infections, or corneal ulcers can lead to scarring and vision loss if treatment is delayed. The American Academy of Ophthalmology notes that corneal abrasions can cause pain, watery eyes, blurry vision, and light sensitivity.

4. Excessive Tearing or Eye Discharge
5. Persistent Redness Around the Cornea

Understanding and Supporting a Family Member with Keratoconus

If a loved one has been diagnosed with Keratoconus, you might be wondering how you can offer the best support. Keratoconus is a condition where the cornea thins and gradually bulges outward into a cone shape, which can significantly affect vision and quality of life. Understanding their challenges and knowing how to help is crucial.

Here’s how you can be a pillar of support:

Educate Yourself: Learn about Keratoconus, its symptoms, and the available treatment options. This helps you empathize and understand what your family member is going through.

Be Patient and Understanding: Simple tasks can become frustrating due to fluctuating vision. Offer patience and practical help with tasks like reading, driving (especially at night), or navigating unfamiliar places.

Living with Keratoconus can be as emotionally challenging as it is physically demanding. If you find yourself experiencing anxiety, frustration, or a sense of isolation due to your vision, please know that you are not alone. It is very common for patients to feel the weight of this diagnosis.

Can Stress Make Keratoconus Worse?

Many patients often ask if lifestyle factors like stress can impact their eye health, particularly those managing Keratoconus.
